public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 951

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/951](https://www.erdosproblems.com/951)
 - [Er77c] Erdős, Paul, Problems and results on combinatorial number theory. III. Number theory day (Proc. Conf., Rockefeller Univ.,
    New York, 1976) (1977), 43-72.
-/

@[expose] public section

open scoped Finsupp Nat.Prime Topology
open Filter

namespace Erdos951

/-- A sequence `a : ℕ → ℝ` is said to have property `Erdos951Prop` if for any pair of distinct
finitely supported sequences `k l : ℕ →₀ ℕ` their corresponding Beurling integers are of distance
at least one apart. -/
def Erdos951Prop (a : ℕ → ℝ) : Prop :=
  ∀ (k ℓ : ℕ →₀ ℕ), k ≠ ℓ → |beurlingInteger a k - beurlingInteger a ℓ| ≥ 1

/-- If a strictly increasing sequence `a : ℕ → ℝ` has property `Erdos951Prop`
and `1 < a 0`, then `a` is a sequence of Beurling prime numbers. -/
@[category API, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_951.variants.isBeurlingPrimes {a : ℕ → ℝ} (ha : 1 < a 0)
    (hm : StrictMono a) (he : Erdos951Prop a) :
    IsBeurlingPrimes a := by
  refine ⟨ha, hm, tendsto_atTop_atTop.2 fun x => ?_⟩
  by_contra h_contra
  obtain ⟨L, hL⟩ : ∃ L, Filter.Tendsto a Filter.atTop (𝓝 L) :=
    ⟨_, tendsto_atTop_isLUB hm.monotone (isLUB_ciSup ⟨x, Set.forall_mem_range.2 fun n =>
    le_of_not_ge fun hn => h_contra ⟨n, fun m hm' => hn.trans (hm.monotone hm')⟩⟩)⟩
  obtain ⟨N, hN⟩ := Metric.tendsto_atTop.mp hL (1 / 2) (by norm_num)
  have := hm (by linarith : N < N + 1)
  have h_diff : a (N + 1) - a N ≥ 1 := by
    rw [← abs_of_nonneg (by linarith : 0 ≤ a _ - _)]
    simpa using he (.single (N + 1) 1) (.single N 1) (by simpa [Finsupp.ext_iff] using ⟨N, by simp⟩)
  linarith [abs_lt.1 (hN N le_rfl), abs_lt.1 (hN (N + 1) (by grind))]

/-- If `1 < a 0 < ...` has property `Erdos951Prop`, is it true that `#{a i ≤ x} ≤ π x`? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_951 : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ a : ℕ → ℝ, 1 < a 0 → StrictMono a → Erdos951Prop a →
      ∀ᶠ (x : ℝ) in Filter.atTop, {i : ℕ | a i ≤ x}.ncard ≤ π ⌊x⌋₊ := by
  sorry

/-- Beurling conjectured that if `1 < a 0 < a 1 < ⋯` has property `Erdos951Prop` and the number
of reals in $[1, x]$ of the form $\prod_i a_i^{k_i}$ is $x + o(\log x)$, then `a` must be the
sequence of primes. Property `Erdos951Prop` makes distinct exponent vectors give distinct
Beurling integers, so counting the set `BeurlingIntegers a` counts the generalised integers. -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_951.variants.beurling :
    ∀ a : ℕ → ℝ, IsBeurlingPrimes a → Erdos951Prop a →
    ((fun x => (BeurlingIntegers a ∩ .Iic x).ncard - x) =o[atTop] Real.log) →
    a = Nat.cast ∘ Nat.nth Nat.Prime := by
  sorry

end Erdos951

findings.description: The premise `Erdos951Prop a` restricts this declaration to unit-separated generalized integers. Erdős's independent restatement of Beurling's conjecture in [Er80] does not impose that premise: he introduces unit separation only afterward, for Shapiro's separate question. Thus the Lean declaration captures a restricted case, not transparently the full Beurling conjecture. This is a scope concern rather than a definite misformalization: the docstring explicitly includes the restriction, and the surrounding discussion in the directly cited [Er77c] and on erdosproblems.com could be read as retaining the main problem's hypotheses. I did not establish an equivalence between the restricted and unrestricted conjectures.
findings.source_evidence: Erdős, 'A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory' (1980), p.103, https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-03.pdf: 'The following nice conjecture is due to Beurling. Let 1 < P₁ < ... be a sequence of real numbers' and assume B(x)=x+o(log x); 'Then the P's are the primes.' The next paragraph separately begins: 'In this connection H.N. Shapiro asked ... Assume that the numbers ... differ by at least one.' Compare [Er77c], pp.68–69, https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1977-27.pdf, and the Beurling remark at https://www.erdosproblems.com/951.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify whether this is intentionally only the unit-separated special case of Beurling's conjecture. If so, identify it as such and provide a reference for its solved status. If the full conjecture is intended, remove the spacing premise and use a multiplicity-aware generalized-integer counting function, such as the cardinality of exponent vectors producing values at most x; simply removing the premise while retaining set-valued counting is not a safe correction.

reformulations.difference: Under its stated spacing hypothesis, Lean counts the set `BeurlingIntegers a ∩ Set.Iic x`, rather than explicitly counting finitely supported exponent vectors whose products lie in [1,x]. It also packages divergence to infinity into `IsBeurlingPrimes`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: All generators exceed 1, so every product is at least 1, including the empty product 1. The spacing condition forces the product map to be injective, making value-counting and exponent-vector counting identical. Bounded product sets are finite: taking the natural floor injects a unit-separated subset of [1,x] into a finite interval of naturals. Consequently neither ncard's infinite-set default nor omission of the lower endpoint changes the count. The existing proved helper derives divergence from the original increasing-sequence and spacing premises. Scratch Lean proofs establish the counting-hypothesis ↔ and the packaged-premises ↔. These equivalences are conditional on spacing and do not settle the separate scope concern above.
